operationalSituations.description: Developer runs rsfusa during local development to check their Rust code
CI/CD pipeline runs rsfusa as an automated gate on pull requests and main branch pushes
Safety auditor reviews evidence bundles produced by rsfusa for certification submission

hazards.description: False negative: rsfusa fails to report a genuine safety rule violation in Rust source code
Wrong ASIL determination: rsfusa derives an incorrect integrity level from configuration parameters
Silent failure: rsfusa encounters an internal error but exits 0, masking the failure from CI
Evidence integrity violation: audit pack contents are tampered with after generation, undetected
Configuration silently disables safety checks through excludePatterns or disposition suppression

safetyGoals.description: rsfusa shall report every safety rule violation — no false negatives in qualified rules
safetyGoals.safeState: the affected rule's qualification is treated as unproven and the CI gate does not pass until qualification is restored

safetyGoals.description: ASIL allocation shall match the configured integrity level per ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 4
safetyGoals.safeState: an ambiguous or unrecognised integrity value is rejected rather than silently defaulted

safetyGoals.description: rsfusa shall exit non-zero on any ERROR finding or internal analysis failure — never exit 0 while masking a real problem
safetyGoals.safeState: the process exits non-zero and CI treats the run as failed rather than passed

safetyGoals.description: Evidence bundles shall include a real SHA-256 hash for every artefact to enable tamper detection
safetyGoals.safeState: an artefact whose recomputed hash disagrees with its recorded hash is treated as untrusted evidence

safetyGoals.description: Suppressing a finding via disposition shall never delete it from the record — it remains visible in check output and in disposition list, and only an accepted/deferred disposition (never a source-scanning exclusion) may exempt it from the exit-code gate
safetyGoals.safeState: an unmatched (orphaned) accepted/deferred disposition is itself reported as a WARNING rather than silently trusted
